Hello Chithanh,

You can use any function that takes a distance matrix as its input and produces a "phylo" object. In the help page for `aboot`, you can find an example that uses other tree methods.

The default upgma method actually is actually defined as

upgma <- function(d) ape::as.phylo(hclust(as.dist(d), method = "average"))

If you want to use ward.D2, you can change the method and define a new function:

wardd2 <- function(d) ape::as.phylo(hclust(as.dist(d), method = "ward.D2"))

and then you can use that in the function like so:

aboot(myData, tree = wardd2, root = TRUE)

I hope that helps.
